name: Stringy Cosmic Strings
description: A straight string with finite energy per unit length, a curved transverse space, and a hidden torus whose shape changes with position around it.
convention: We take components in $x^0=ct$, and use the length $\ell$ as the unit in the drawings.
history: A hidden torus changes shape from place to place around a straight string. After a circuit of the string, the two cycles of the torus can return relabelled, leaving the same physical torus [greene1990stringy]. Brian R. Greene, Alfred D. Shapere, Cumrun Vafa, and Shing-Tung Yau introduced these stringy cosmic strings in 1990 [greene1990stringy]. The torus is part of the compact space at each point of the four dimensional spacetime [greene1990stringy].¶Write $z=x+iy$ for position across the string and $\tau=\tau_1+i\tau_2$ for the shape of the torus ($\tau_2>0$). The four dimensional line element is $ds^2=-dt^2+dw^2+H(z,\bar z)\,dz\,d\bar z$, with $w$ along the string [harveyroyston2008]. For simple poles at $z_i$, the transverse factor is $H=\tau_2|\eta(\tau)|^4\prod_i|z-z_i|^{-1/6}$ [harveyroyston2008]. The function $\eta$ is the Dedekind eta function.¶The shape obeys $j(\tau(z))=P(z)/Q(z)$, where $P$ and $Q$ are coprime polynomials [harveyroyston2008]. The modular invariant $j$ has the normalization $j(i)=1$. In this normalization, zeros of $P$ have multiplicity divisible by three and zeros of $P-Q$ have even multiplicity, so that $\tau$ is holomorphic at $j=0$ and $j=1$ [harveyroyston2008].¶The energy per unit length of an isolated straight string of a broken global $U(1)$ symmetry grows logarithmically with distance from its core [steinschabesburd1988]. For stringy cosmic strings, the identification of torus shapes under $SL(2,\mathbb Z)$ permits finite energy per unit length [greene1990stringy]. Near a simple pole, the eta factor cancels the explicit power of $|z-z_i|$ in $H$, leaving logarithmic growth from $\tau_2$ [greene1990stringy, harveyroyston2008]. The reduced metric becomes singular at degeneration points of the torus [greene1990stringy].¶Far from $N$ simple poles, with $\tau$ approaching a finite value, the transverse factor obeys $H\sim |z|^{-N/6}$ [gibbonsgreenperry1996]. Each pole contributes $\pi/6$ to the asymptotic angular deficit [gibbonsgreenperry1996]. Twelve poles give a cylindrical end, and twenty four poles close the transverse space into a 2-sphere [greene1990stringy, gibbonsgreenperry1996]. The regular holomorphic family has six, twelve, or twenty four poles [harveyroyston2008]. The torus over the sphere forms an elliptic K3 surface [greene1990stringy]. The K3 surface admits a smooth Ricci-flat metric; the displayed reduced metric applies away from the degeneration regions [greene1990stringy].¶Miho Marui and Kiyoshi Shiraishi obtained a related solution preserving half the supersymmetry in five dimensional supergravity in 1991 [maruishiraishi1991]. Paul S. Green and Tristan Hübsch replaced the torus by a Calabi-Yau threefold in 1994, obtaining strings at conifold degenerations [greenhubsch1994]. The metric factor stays finite at those cores, and the curvature diverges logarithmically [greenhubsch1994]. Ashoke Sen related the fundamental string to the local stringy cosmic string by a duality transformation after reduction to three dimensions in 1995 [sen1995duality]. Several torus moduli can vary together; one, two, or three varying moduli preserve one half, one quarter, or one eighth of the supersymmetry in four dimensional $N=4$ supergravity [duff1995dualstrings]. The complex structure string also belongs to the family of $S$, $T$, and $U$ strings related by heterotic and type II dualities [duff1996triality].¶Gary W. Gibbons, Michael B. Green, and Malcolm J. Perry obtained the same transverse geometry for seven branes in type IIB supergravity in 1996 [gibbonsgreenperry1996]. The scalar $\tau$ then combines the axion and dilaton [gibbonsgreenperry1996]. Eric A. Bergshoeff and coauthors found circular seven brane geometries related by T-duality to type IIA six and eight branes in 1996 [bergshoeff1996duality]. Vafa encoded this scalar as the shape of an auxiliary torus in F-theory, with its area frozen [vafa1996ftheory]. Sen identified a constant $\tau$ limit with four groups of six seven branes and a transverse $T^2/\mathbb Z_2$ geometry [sen1996orientifolds]. Hirosi Ooguri and Vafa gave a smooth local elliptic metric whose corrections to the reduced metric decay exponentially away from a simple degeneration [oogurivafa1996].¶Alexandros Kehagias extended the modular construction to heterotic theories with several varying moduli in a 1996 preprint [kehagias1996]. Masako Asano wrote down metrics for F-theory bases formed from two 2-spheres in 1997 [asano1997]. Alok Kumar and Vafa extended the monodromies to larger duality groups and auxiliary tori of higher dimension in 1997 [kumarvafa1997]. James T. Liu and Ruben Minasian obtained local equations for overlapping fivebranes and special Lagrangian 3-torus fibrations in 1998 [liuminasian1998]. Kumar and Aalok Misra derived supersymmetry conditions for networks of $T$ and $U$ strings in 2000; compatible spatial and internal orientations preserve one quarter of the supersymmetry [kumarmisra2000].¶Eduardo Eyras and Yolanda Lozano constructed a source action for the S-dual seven brane and related its local geometry to the D7 geometry by a transverse coordinate change in 2000 [eyraslozano2000]. Martin B. Einhorn and Leopoldo A. Pando Zayas placed several local magnetic seven brane geometries in a family with one free parameter in the radial conformal factor in 2000 [einhornpandozayas2000]. The scalar is holomorphic in the supersymmetric family [einhornpandozayas2000]. Ernesto Lozano-Tellechea and Tomás Ortín obtained a chain of branes with compact isometric directions that share the reduced transverse metric in 2001 [lozanotellecheaortin2001]. Bergshoeff, Ulf Gran, and Diederik Roest found local seven brane solutions in three conjugacy classes of $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ in 2002 [bergshoeffgranroest2002]. Constant scalar limits include conical geometries with nontrivial fermion monodromy; the general local solutions require a global completion to have finite energy [bergshoeffgranroest2002].¶Simeon Hellerman, John McGreevy, and Brook Williams allowed both the shape and complexified area of a torus to vary in 2004 [hellerman2004]. Neighbouring regions can then join through T-duality transformations that mix the metric and antisymmetric tensor field [hellerman2004]. Each modulus has twelve degeneration points on the transverse 2-sphere in the compact model [hellerman2004]. Ling-Yan Hung constructed local intersecting D7-brane geometries with the axion and dilaton varying over two complex coordinates in 2007 [hung2007]. Bergshoeff and coauthors imposed global Killing spinor monodromy on seven brane configurations that include additional conical sources [bergshoeff2007sevenbranes].¶Jeffrey A. Harvey and Andrew B. Royston studied D3-branes crossing the compact seven brane geometry in 2008 [harveyroyston2008]. Chiral fermion zero modes on the D3-branes occur in the compact case [harveyroyston2008]. Bergshoeff and coauthors coupled stringy cosmic strings to two form potentials dual to scalar isometries in four dimensional $N=2$ supergravity [bergshoeff2008strings]. The vector strings and hyperstrings preserve half the supersymmetry [bergshoeff2008strings]. Ortín obtained holomorphic cosmic strings within the supersymmetric solutions of ungauged matter coupled $N=1$ supergravity [ortin2008].¶David Vegh and McGreevy built compactifications with networks of 3-torus degenerations in 2008 [veghmcgreevy2008]. Some of these compactifications admit an asymmetric orbifold description [veghmcgreevy2008]. Dieter Lüst, Stefano Massai, and Valentí Vall Camell gave local torus fibrations with parabolic, elliptic, and hyperbolic T-duality monodromies in 2016 [lust2016tfolds]. A torus fibration patched by T-duality transformations is called a T-fold [lust2016tfolds]. The hyperbolic solutions require a finite cutoff before the imaginary part of the modulus changes sign [lust2016tfolds].¶Lüst, Erik Plauschinn, and Vall Camell followed changes in string momentum and winding around torus degenerations in 2017 [lust2017unwinding]. Local double field theory geometries depend on coordinates conjugate to winding [lust2017unwinding]. Ismail Achmed-Zade, Mark J. D. Hamilton, Lüst, and Massai wrote down global monodromy data for 3-torus T-folds over a punctured 2-sphere in 2018 [achmedzade2018]. The monodromies act geometrically on a 4-torus fiber [achmedzade2018]. Achmed-Zade and coauthors argued that additional winding modes enter the local string description near a defect [achmedzade2018].¶Fernando Marchesano and Max Wiesner constructed globally completed axionic string examples in four dimensions in 2022 [marchesanowiesner2022]. Additional strings with noncommuting monodromies regulate the scalar profile at large distance [marchesanowiesner2022]. Marchesano and Wiesner conjectured that such completions exist for a broader class of effective strings [marchesanowiesner2022]. Wiesner related regulator strings to strong coupling singularities in $N=1$ F-theory models with heterotic duals in 2023 [wiesner2023]. A nonzero scalar potential can change the holomorphic profiles of these strings [wiesner2023].¶Keren Chen, Qinjian Lou, and Yi-Nan Wang calculated massive string junctions and the Kaluza-Klein spectrum of the two form potentials on compact seven brane geometries in 2025 [chenlouwang2025]. Two groups containing twelve elementary seven branes in total can collide at fixed base volume and locally constant axion and dilaton [chenlouwang2025]. The string junctions connecting those groups form an infinite tower whose masses tend to zero [chenlouwang2025].¶José Calderón-Infante and coauthors found a positively divergent scalar potential after reducing the D7 geometry on its angular circle in a 2026 preprint [calderoninfante2026]. Naoto Kan, Masashi Kawahira, and Hiroki Wada applied the transverse modular construction to a scalar truncation of type 0B gravity in a 2026 preprint [kankawahirawada2026]. Eight seven branes with $\mathbb Z_4$ charge form a compact example with constant scalar ($\tau=(1+i)/2$) and monodromy in $\Gamma_0(2)$ [kankawahirawada2026]. The closed string tachyon remains unstable in this background [kankawahirawada2026].

related.text: The exterior of the Vilenkin-Gott string is a flat cone, and the stringy cosmic string has a curved transverse space that approaches a cone far away [gott1985, gibbonsgreenperry1996].
A point particle removes a wedge from a flat plane, and enough particles close space on itself [deser1984, gibbonsgreenperry1996].
A global monopole's scalar field spreads its energy away from its core, and the stringy cosmic string also carries a scalar field across its transverse space [barriola1989, vafa1996ftheory].
A compact direction changes over space around the Kaluza-Klein monopole, and a compact torus changes shape around the stringy cosmic string [sorkin1983, vafa1996ftheory].

parameters.description: Positive transverse factor fixed by the torus shape and the string positions.

coordinates.convention: We use $(t,w,x,y)$ with $x$ and $y$ across the string and $z=x+iy$. Six coincident strings have constant shape in the spacetime and embedding diagrams.
